site.name: meadowid
site.summary: MeadowID — identity dashboard (local demo) Fictional unified-identity dashboard. Local fixture for UXBench. Open `index.html` directly. Pages `index.html` — Overview Sidebar nav plus a four-tile stat row (Connected apps, Active sessions, Passkeys, Trust score), an "issues" alert list (unfamiliar session, weak factor, stale app), a recent sign-in ledger, and a recovery-readiness checklist. `connected-apps.html` — Connected apps Filterable / searchable list of every app that holds a token on the user's behalf. Each card shows scope chips (sensitive ones highlighted) and a Revoke button that requires confirmation. `devices.html` — Active sessions

run_plan.goal: Exhaustively validate MeadowID’s primary identity-security settings flow and adjacent recovery paths across all known pages, with emphasis on risk actions, confirmation states, and mobile usability.
run_plan.summary: Start from the overview dashboard, then follow the strongest security-related prompts into sessions, passkeys, connected apps, export, and freeze flows. Treat the dashboard alerts and recovery readiness widgets as navigation cues to deeper pages, and validate that destructive or high-impact actions require appropriate confirmation. Repeat the critical paths in a mobile viewport to check whether the many small tap targets and compact sidebar links remain usable.
assumptions: The app is a local demo with no real backend side effects, but UI state changes and confirmation steps should still be exercised.
All meaningful user journeys are reachable from the six known HTML pages plus the sidebar and in-page links/buttons already observed.
Profile and Billing links shown in the sidebar are placeholders (#) and should not be treated as functional pages unless the browser reveals otherwise.
risk_hotspots: index.html: 'Run security check' button and alert actions ('Dismiss all', 'Review', 'Add passkey', 'Open', 'Configure', 'verify now')
devices.html: 'End all other sessions' and the unfamiliar Reykjavík session row/pin interactions
connected-apps.html: search/filter/sort controls and per-app 'Revoke' confirmation, especially on sensitive scopes
passkeys.html: 'Remove', 'Re-pair', 'Reveal & download', and recovery email/passkey state management
data-export.html: multi-step export wizard, checkboxes/options, and final request/continue path
freeze.html: freeze switch and the permanently sensitive 'Request deletion' adjacent flow
Mobile viewport: all sidebar nav items and compact action buttons flagged with small tap target warnings

phases.title: Dashboard triage and navigation map
phases.objective: Validate the overview page as the control center and use its alerts/cards to reach the adjacent security pages.
key_checks: Inspect the four summary tiles and confirm the dashboard conveys a coherent security posture (connected apps, sessions, passkeys, trust score, recovery email state).
Exercise the primary action 'Run security check' and observe whether it changes state, opens a result, or remains a no-op in the demo.
Follow each prominent dashboard CTA at least once: Review, Add passkey, Open, See all, Configure, verify now, and Dismiss all if it is active.
Confirm the sidebar navigation routes cleanly to every known page.
exit_criteria: All dashboard CTAs have been tested or determined to be inert/placeholders.
The run has a confirmed route to each of the five adjacent security pages.

phases.title: Active sessions review
phases.objective: Validate the session-management page, its current-session indicator, and the remediation action for unfamiliar devices.
key_checks: Open the Active sessions page and inspect the list structure, labels, and the selected current device state.
Test the 'End all other sessions' control and verify whether a confirmation or state change occurs.
Inspect the unfamiliar Reykjavík session and any row/pin affordances to ensure the warning is actionable and understandable.
Check whether clicking rows reveals detail such as factor, app, start time, or location.
exit_criteria: The current-session state and at least one unfamiliar-session remediation path have been validated.
Any destructive action has been confirmed to require the appropriate safeguard or is noted as missing.

phases.title: Connected apps token management
phases.objective: Validate search, category/sort controls, app cards, and token revocation behavior for connected integrations.
key_checks: Exercise the search field with at least one query and confirm results/filtering behavior.
Change category and sort controls to verify the list updates and the labels remain understandable.
Open several app cards and inspect scope chips, especially sensitive scopes and any highlighted permissions.
Use a Revoke action on at least one app and verify confirmation, cancellation, and post-action state if available.
exit_criteria: Search, filter, sort, and revoke flows have each been exercised at least once.
At least one sensitive-scope app card has been inspected in detail.

phases.title: Passkeys, backup factors, and recovery setup
phases.objective: Validate authentication-strengthening and account-recovery management, including removal and reveal actions.
key_checks: Inspect the list of active passkeys and confirm the active/inactive semantics are clear.
Test 'Add a passkey' and observe the expected setup entry point or placeholder behavior.
Exercise 'Remove' on at least one passkey and verify any warning, confirmation, or irreversible language.
Test 'Re-pair' for the TOTP backup factor and 'Reveal & download' for backup codes.
Validate recovery email interaction via the visible input and 'Send verification' control, plus the trusted contact field if editable.
exit_criteria: At least one passkey action, one backup-factor action, and one recovery-action path have been checked.
The risk of being locked out by removing factors is clearly represented or flagged if not.

phases.title: Export data wizard and consent boundaries
phases.objective: Validate the export flow as a multi-step process with category selection, format/filter options, scheduling, and review.
key_checks: Walk through the multi-step wizard headings in order and confirm the current step is clear.
Toggle a representative subset of export categories, including high-volume and sensitive categories such as sign-in history, security audit log, and billing/receipts.
Inspect the format/filter and schedule controls for clarity and default safety.
Test Back, Save as draft, and Continue to confirm progression and recovery from mistakes.
exit_criteria: The wizard’s step structure and at least one end-to-end progression path are covered.
Sensitive category selection and export size implications have been observed.

phases.title: Freeze and account-level escalation
phases.objective: Validate the strongest account control, its explanatory copy, and adjacent irreversible actions.
key_checks: Review the freeze explanation for clarity around what is paused, blocked, or preserved.
Inspect the freeze switch behavior and any confirm/cancel pattern if present.
Follow the adjacent 'Request deletion' link or entry point and note whether it is clearly distinguished from freeze.
Check that the user is warned about unfreezing requirements and third-party side effects.
exit_criteria: The freeze flow has been inspected for user clarity and safety.
Any irreversible or high-risk adjacent path has been identified and separated from reversible freeze state.

coverage_targets.pages: visit all known HTML pages: index, connected-apps, devices, passkeys, data-export, freeze
coverage_targets.features: exercise most visible controls on each page, including at least one control per major action group and one destructive/high-risk action where available
coverage_targets.mobile: repeat critical checks on mobile viewport, prioritizing sidebar navigation, dashboard CTAs, revoke/end-session/freeze actions, and any controls flagged with small tap target warnings

notes: Known UX risk: many sidebar and action controls are already flagged as small tap targets; mobile validation should explicitly check whether this impacts discoverability and precision.
Avoid spending steps on placeholder links such as Profile and Billing unless the page unexpectedly resolves to real content.
If a control opens a modal or confirmation, prefer testing both confirm and cancel paths when safe within the step budget.

prescan_summary.title: Freeze account — MeadowID
prescan_summary.visible_text_excerpt: MeadowID ◐ Overview ⇄ Connected apps ▢ Active sessions ⌘ Passkeys & 2FA ↓ Export your data ❄ Freeze account JT Jamal Tarrant jamal@thirdpond.dev Freeze account A freeze is the strongest, reversible version of "stop everything." We use it for incidents. It is not the same as deleting your account. What freezing does Every connected app is signed out and rejected until you unfreeze. New tokens cannot be issued. Sign-ins are blocked from every device. You'll need your password and a passkey or backup code to unfreeze. Subscriptions, automatic backups, and recurring data exports are paused. Your data is not deleted. Nothing is shared with apps. You stay billed only if a free trial is converting. What freezing does not do It does not remove sessions on third-party servers that don't honor token revocation (extremely rare; we report these). It does not freeze accounts you opened with email/pas

observation.title: Freeze account — MeadowID
observation.visible_text: MeadowID ◐ Overview ⇄ Connected apps ▢ Active sessions ⌘ Passkeys & 2FA ↓ Export your data ❄ Freeze account JT Jamal Tarrant jamal@thirdpond.dev Freeze account A freeze is the strongest, reversible version of "stop everything." We use it for incidents. It is not the same as deleting your account. What freezing does Every connected app is signed out and rejected until you unfreeze. New tokens cannot be issued. Sign-ins are blocked from every device. You'll need your password and a passkey or backup code to unfreeze. Subscriptions, automatic backups, and recurring data exports are paused. Your data is not deleted. Nothing is shared with apps. You stay billed only if a free trial is converting. What freezing does not do It does not remove sessions on third-party servers that don't honor token revocation (extremely rare; we report these). It does not freeze accounts you opened with email/password and never linked to MeadowID. Freeze switch Once you flip this, every device will be signed out within 60 seconds. Make sure you can unfreeze: have your password and a passkey (or printed backup codes) on hand. If you only have SMS as a second factor, set up something stronger first. Not frozen Need something more permanent? If you're leaving the platform for good, request full deletion. We'll require email confirmation and a 7-day cool-off window before we wipe. Request deletion Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

observation.title: Freeze account — MeadowID
observation.visible_text: MeadowID ◐ Overview ⇄ Connected apps ▢ Active sessions ⌘ Passkeys & 2FA ↓ Export your data ❄ Freeze account JT Jamal Tarrant jamal@thirdpond.dev Freeze account A freeze is the strongest, reversible version of "stop everything." We use it for incidents. It is not the same as deleting your account. What freezing does Every connected app is signed out and rejected until you unfreeze. New tokens cannot be issued. Sign-ins are blocked from every device. You'll need your password and a passkey or backup code to unfreeze. Subscriptions, automatic backups, and recurring data exports are paused. Your data is not deleted. Nothing is shared with apps. You stay billed only if a free trial is converting. What freezing does not do It does not remove sessions on third-party servers that don't honor token revocation (extremely rare; we report these). It does not freeze accounts you opened with email/password and never linked to MeadowID. Freeze switch Once you flip this, every device will be signed out within 60 seconds. Make sure you can unfreeze: have your password and a passkey (or printed backup codes) on hand. If you only have SMS as a second factor, set up something stronger first. Not frozen Need something more permanent? If you're leaving the platform for good, request full deletion. We'll require email confirmation and a 7-day cool-off window before we wipe. Request deletion Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

Request deletion Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.
